raw: Act 3, Scene 1 — A public Place

summary.en: Tybalt wants to fight Romeo, but Romeo refuses. Mercutio fights instead and is killed. Romeo kills Tybalt, and the Prince banishes Romeo.

raw: Enter Mercutio, Benvolio, Page and Servants.

sentences.en: Mercutio, Benvolio, a Page, and Servants enter.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
I pray thee, good Mercutio, let’s retire:
The day is hot, the Capulets abroad,
And if we meet, we shall not scape a brawl,
For now these hot days, is the mad blood stirring.

sentences.en: Please, good Mercutio, let us go home.
The day is hot.
The Capulets are out and about.
If we meet them, we will not escape a fight.
These hot days make people's blood boil and make them angry.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Thou art like one of these fellows that, when he enters the confines of
a tavern, claps me his sword upon the table, and says ‘God send me no
need of thee!’ and by the operation of the second cup draws him on the
drawer, when indeed there is no need.

sentences.en: You are like one of those men.
When they enter a tavern, they put their sword on the table.
They say, 'God send me no need of you!'
After the second drink, they draw their sword on the barman.
They do this even when there is no need for it.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Am I like such a fellow?

sentences.en: Am I like such a man?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Come, come, thou art as hot a Jack in thy mood as any in Italy; and as
soon moved to be moody, and as soon moody to be moved.

sentences.en: Come, come, you are as hot-headed as any man in Italy.
You get angry very quickly.
And you become calm just as quickly.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: And what to?

sentences.en: Moved to what?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Nay, an there were two such, we should have none shortly, for one would
kill the other. Thou? Why, thou wilt quarrel with a man that hath a
hair more or a hair less in his beard than thou hast. Thou wilt quarrel
with a man for cracking nuts, having no other reason but because thou
hast hazel eyes. What eye but such an eye would spy out such a quarrel?
Thy head is as full of quarrels as an egg is full of meat, and yet thy
head hath been beaten as addle as an egg for quarrelling. Thou hast
quarrelled with a man for coughing in the street, because he hath
wakened thy dog that hath lain asleep in the sun. Didst thou not fall
out with a tailor for wearing his new doublet before Easter? with
another for tying his new shoes with an old riband? And yet thou wilt
tutor me from quarrelling!

sentences.en: No, if there were two such men, we would have none of them soon.
One would kill the other.
You? You would fight a man who has one hair more or less in his beard than you.
You would fight a man for cracking nuts.
You would do this for no reason other than because you have hazel eyes.
What eye but such an eye would find such a fight?
Your head is as full of fights as an egg is full of meat.
Yet your head has been beaten as soft as an egg from fighting.
You fought a man for coughing in the street.
He had woken up your dog that was sleeping in the sun.
Did you not fight with a tailor for wearing his new jacket before Easter?
Did you not fight with another for tying his new shoes with an old ribbon?
And yet you want to tell me not to fight!

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
And I were so apt to quarrel as thou art, any man should buy the fee
simple of my life for an hour and a quarter.

sentences.en: Suppose I were as ready to fight as you are.
Then any man could buy full ownership of my life for an hour and a quarter.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: The fee simple! O simple!

sentences.en: Full ownership!
How simple-minded!

raw: Enter Tybalt and others.

sentences.en: Tybalt and others enter.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: By my head, here comes the Capulets.

sentences.en: By my head, here come the Capulets.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: By my heel, I care not.

sentences.en: By my heel, I do not care.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
Follow me close, for I will speak to them.
Gentlemen, good-den: a word with one of you.

sentences.en: Follow me closely because I will speak to them.
Good evening, gentlemen; I want a word with one of you.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
And but one word with one of us? Couple it with something; make it a
word and a blow.

sentences.en: Only one word with one of us?
Add something else to it.
Make it a word and a blow.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
You shall find me apt enough to that, sir, and you will give me
occasion.

sentences.en: You will find me ready enough for that, sir, if you give me a reason.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Could you not take some occasion without giving?

sentences.en: Could you not take a reason without being given one?

speaker: TYBALT
raw: Mercutio, thou consortest with Romeo.

sentences.en: Mercutio, you are spending time with Romeo.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Consort? What, dost thou make us minstrels? And thou make minstrels of
us, look to hear nothing but discords. Here’s my fiddlestick, here’s
that shall make you dance. Zounds, consort!

sentences.en: Spend time? What, do you think we are musicians?
If you make us musicians, expect to hear only bad notes.
You will only hear unpleasant sounds.
This sword is my fiddle stick.
Here is what will make you dance.
Damn it, 'spend time'!

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
We talk here in the public haunt of men.
Either withdraw unto some private place,
And reason coldly of your grievances,
Or else depart; here all eyes gaze on us.

sentences.en: We are talking here in a public place.
Either go to a private place.
Talk about your problems calmly there.
Or leave now.
Everyone is looking at us here.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Men’s eyes were made to look, and let them gaze.
I will not budge for no man’s pleasure, I.

sentences.en: Men's eyes were made to look.
Let them look.
I will not move for any man's pleasure.

raw: Enter Romeo.

speaker: TYBALT
raw: Well, peace be with you, sir, here comes my man.

sentences.en: Well, peace be with you, sir.
Here comes my man.

speaker: MERCUTIO

sentences.en: But I will be hanged if he wears your uniform.
But go to the dueling field first.
He will follow you there.
Only in that sense can you call him your man.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
Romeo, the love I bear thee can afford
No better term than this: Thou art a villain.

sentences.en: Romeo, the love I have for you allows no better word than this.
You are a villain.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Tybalt, the reason that I have to love thee
Doth much excuse the appertaining rage
To such a greeting. Villain am I none;
Therefore farewell; I see thou know’st me not.

sentences.en: Tybalt, I have a reason to love you.
It lets me forgive the anger I should feel at such a greeting.
I am not a villain.
Therefore goodbye.
I see that you do not know me.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
Boy, this shall not excuse the injuries
That thou hast done me, therefore turn and draw.

sentences.en: Boy, this will not excuse the injuries you have done to me.
Therefore turn and draw your sword.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
I do protest I never injur’d thee,
But love thee better than thou canst devise
Till thou shalt know the reason of my love.
And so good Capulet, which name I tender
As dearly as mine own, be satisfied.

sentences.en: I protest that I never hurt you.
I love you more than you can imagine.
You will see this when you know the reason for my love.
And since I value the name Capulet as much as my own, be satisfied.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: O calm, dishonourable, vile submission!

sentences.en: Oh, what a calm, dishonorable, and vile submission!

raw: Draws.

sentences.en: Mercutio draws his sword.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Alla stoccata carries it away.
Tybalt, you rat-catcher, will you walk?

sentences.en: So this fancy fighting man wins, does he?
Tybalt, you rat-catcher, will you come and fight?

speaker: TYBALT
raw: What wouldst thou have with me?

sentences.en: What do you want from me?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Good King of Cats, nothing but one of your nine lives; that I mean to
make bold withal, and, as you shall use me hereafter, dry-beat the rest
of the eight. Will you pluck your sword out of his pilcher by the ears?
Make haste, lest mine be about your ears ere it be out.

sentences.en: Good King of Cats, I only need one of your nine lives.
I intend to be bold with it.
And then I will beat the other eight out of you.
Will you pull your sword out of its case by the ears?
Hurry, or my sword will be around your ears before yours is out.

raw: Drawing.

sentences.en: Tybalt draws his sword.

speaker: TYBALT
raw: I am for you.

sentences.en: I am ready to fight you.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Gentle Mercutio, put thy rapier up.

sentences.en: Gentle Mercutio, put your sword away.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw: Come, sir, your passado.

sentences.en: Come, sir, show me your fancy move.

raw: They fight.

sentences.en: They fight.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Draw, Benvolio; beat down their weapons.
Gentlemen, for shame, forbear this outrage,
Tybalt, Mercutio, the Prince expressly hath
Forbid this bandying in Verona streets.
Hold, Tybalt! Good Mercutio!

sentences.en: Draw, Benvolio, and beat down their weapons.
Gentlemen, stop this violence for shame!
Tybalt, Mercutio, the Prince has strictly forbidden fighting in the streets of Verona.
Stop, Tybalt! Good Mercutio!

raw: Exeunt Tybalt with his Partizans.

sentences.en: Tybalt runs off with his followers.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
I am hurt.
A plague o’ both your houses. I am sped.
Is he gone, and hath nothing?

sentences.en: I am hurt. A plague on both your houses.
I am dying. Is he gone without a scratch?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: What, art thou hurt?

sentences.en: What, are you hurt?

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Ay, ay, a scratch, a scratch. Marry, ’tis enough.
Where is my page? Go villain, fetch a surgeon.

sentences.en: Yes, yes, it is just a scratch; it is enough.
Where is my servant? Go, boy, and get a doctor.

raw: Exit Page.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: Courage, man; the hurt cannot be much.

sentences.en: Be brave, man.
The injury cannot be very bad.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
No, ’tis not so deep as a well, nor so wide as a church door, but ’tis
enough, ’twill serve. Ask for me tomorrow, and you shall find me a
grave man. I am peppered, I warrant, for this world. A plague o’ both
your houses. Zounds, a dog, a rat, a mouse, a cat, to scratch a man to
death. A braggart, a rogue, a villain, that fights by the book of
arithmetic!—Why the devil came you between us? I was hurt under your
arm.

sentences.en: No, it is not as deep as a well or as wide as a church door.
But it is enough; it will do.
Ask for me tomorrow, and you will find me a grave man lying in my grave.
I am finished in this world, I promise. A plague on both your houses.
To think a dog, a rat, a mouse, or a cat could scratch a man to death!
He is a show-off and a rogue; he is a villain who fights by a math textbook!
Why did you come between us? I was hurt under your arm.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: I thought all for the best.

sentences.en: I thought it was for the best.

speaker: MERCUTIO
raw:
Help me into some house, Benvolio,
Or I shall faint. A plague o’ both your houses.
They have made worms’ meat of me.
I have it, and soundly too. Your houses!

sentences.en: Help me into a house, Benvolio, or I will faint.
A plague on both your houses!
They have made me food for worms.
I have got it, and badly too.
Your houses!

raw: Exeunt Mercutio and Benvolio.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
This gentleman, the Prince’s near ally,
My very friend, hath got his mortal hurt
In my behalf; my reputation stain’d
With Tybalt’s slander,—Tybalt, that an hour
Hath been my cousin. O sweet Juliet,
Thy beauty hath made me effeminate
And in my temper soften’d valour’s steel.

sentences.en: This gentleman is the Prince's close relative.
He is my very friend.
He suffered a fatal injury for me.
My reputation is ruined by Tybalt's lies.
Tybalt has been my cousin for only an hour!
Oh sweet Juliet, your beauty has made me weak.
It softened my brave spirit.

raw: Re-enter Benvolio.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
O Romeo, Romeo, brave Mercutio’s dead,
That gallant spirit hath aspir’d the clouds,
Which too untimely here did scorn the earth.

sentences.en: Oh Romeo, Romeo, brave Mercutio is dead.
His brave spirit has gone up to the clouds.
He left the earth far too early.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
This day’s black fate on mo days doth depend;
This but begins the woe others must end.

sentences.en: This day's dark fate will hang over more days to come.
This only begins the sadness that others must end.

raw: Re-enter Tybalt.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Here comes the furious Tybalt back again.

sentences.en: The angry Tybalt is coming back here.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Again in triumph, and Mercutio slain?
Away to heaven respective lenity,
And fire-ey’d fury be my conduct now!
Now, Tybalt, take the ‘villain’ back again
That late thou gav’st me, for Mercutio’s soul
Is but a little way above our heads,
Staying for thine to keep him company.
Either thou or I, or both, must go with him.

sentences.en: He is alive and winning, and Mercutio is dead?
I will not be gentle now.
I will act with fire and anger!
Now, Tybalt, take back the 'villain' title.
You gave me that name recently.
Mercutio's soul is just above our heads.
He is waiting for your soul to join him.
Either you or I, or both of us, must go with him.

speaker: TYBALT
raw:
Thou wretched boy, that didst consort him here,
Shalt with him hence.

sentences.en: You miserable boy, you were his friend here.
So you will go with him to death.

speaker: ROMEO
raw: This shall determine that.

sentences.en: This will decide that.

raw: They fight; Tybalt falls.

sentences.en: They fight.
Tybalt falls.

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Romeo, away, be gone!
The citizens are up, and Tybalt slain.
Stand not amaz’d. The Prince will doom thee death
If thou art taken. Hence, be gone, away!

sentences.en: Romeo, go away! The citizens are up in arms.
Tybalt is killed, so do not stand there in shock.
The Prince will sentence you to death if he catches you.
Go away now!

speaker: ROMEO
raw: O, I am fortune’s fool!

sentences.en: Oh, I am a plaything of fate!

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: Why dost thou stay?

sentences.en: Why do you stay?

raw: Exit Romeo.
Enter Citizens.

sentences.en: Citizens enter.

speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
raw:
Which way ran he that kill’d Mercutio?
Tybalt, that murderer, which way ran he?

sentences.en: In which direction did the man who killed Mercutio run?
Tybalt, that murderer, which way did he run?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw: There lies that Tybalt.

sentences.en: That is Tybalt lying there.

speaker: FIRST CITIZEN
raw:
Up, sir, go with me.
I charge thee in the Prince’s name obey.

sentences.en: Get up, sir.
Come with me.
I command you in the Prince's name to obey.

raw: Enter Prince, attended; Montague, Capulet, their Wives and others.

sentences.en: The Prince enters with his followers.
Montague, Capulet, their wives, and others enter.

speaker: PRINCE
raw: Where are the vile beginners of this fray?

sentences.en: Where are the people who started this fight?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
O noble Prince, I can discover all
The unlucky manage of this fatal brawl.
There lies the man, slain by young Romeo,
That slew thy kinsman, brave Mercutio.

sentences.en: Noble Prince, I can explain everything.
I can tell you how this deadly fight happened.
There lies the man who killed your relative, brave Mercutio.
Young Romeo killed him.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
Tybalt, my cousin! O my brother’s child!
O Prince! O husband! O, the blood is spill’d
Of my dear kinsman! Prince, as thou art true,
For blood of ours shed blood of Montague.
O cousin, cousin.

sentences.en: Tybalt, my nephew! He is my brother's child!
O Prince! O husband! The blood of my dear relative is spilled!
Prince, if you are fair, shed Montague blood for ours.
O cousin, cousin.

speaker: PRINCE
raw: Benvolio, who began this bloody fray?

sentences.en: Benvolio, who started this bloody fight?

speaker: BENVOLIO
raw:
Tybalt, here slain, whom Romeo’s hand did slay;
Romeo, that spoke him fair, bid him bethink
How nice the quarrel was, and urg’d withal
Your high displeasure. All this uttered
With gentle breath, calm look, knees humbly bow’d
Could not take truce with the unruly spleen
Of Tybalt, deaf to peace, but that he tilts
With piercing steel at bold Mercutio’s breast,
Who, all as hot, turns deadly point to point,
And, with a martial scorn, with one hand beats
Cold death aside, and with the other sends
It back to Tybalt, whose dexterity
Retorts it. Romeo he cries aloud,
‘Hold, friends! Friends, part!’ and swifter than his tongue,
His agile arm beats down their fatal points,
And ’twixt them rushes; underneath whose arm
An envious thrust from Tybalt hit the life
Of stout Mercutio, and then Tybalt fled.
But by and by comes back to Romeo,
Who had but newly entertain’d revenge,
And to’t they go like lightning; for, ere I
Could draw to part them was stout Tybalt slain;
And as he fell did Romeo turn and fly.
This is the truth, or let Benvolio die.

sentences.en: Tybalt is lying here, and Romeo's hand killed him.
Romeo spoke to him nicely and told Tybalt how bad the fight was.
He warned him about your anger with a gentle voice and a calm look.
He even bowed humbly, but Tybalt did not listen to peace.
Tybalt had an angry temper and attacked Mercutio's chest with a sharp sword.
Mercutio was also very angry, so he fought back with his sword.
He pushed death away with one hand and sent the attack back to Tybalt with the other.
Tybalt blocked the move skillfully while Romeo shouted, 'Stop, friends! Friends, break it up!'
His arm moved faster than his words as he pushed their swords down.
He ran between them, but under his arm, a sneaky thrust from Tybalt struck brave Mercutio.
Then Tybalt ran away, but in a moment, he came back to Romeo.
Romeo had just started to seek revenge, and they fought like lightning.
Before I could move to separate them, Tybalt was killed.
As he fell, Romeo turned and ran away.
This is the truth; if it is not true, let me die.

speaker: LADY CAPULET
raw:
He is a kinsman to the Montague.
Affection makes him false, he speaks not true.
Some twenty of them fought in this black strife,
And all those twenty could but kill one life.
I beg for justice, which thou, Prince, must give;
Romeo slew Tybalt, Romeo must not live.

sentences.en: He is a relative of the Montague family.
Love makes him dishonest, so he does not speak the truth.
About twenty people fought in this terrible fight, but they could only kill one person.
I ask for justice, which you must give, Prince.
Romeo killed Tybalt, so Romeo must not live.

speaker: PRINCE
raw:
Romeo slew him, he slew Mercutio.
Who now the price of his dear blood doth owe?

sentences.en: Romeo killed him.
He killed Mercutio.
Who now owes the price for his dear blood?

speaker: MONTAGUE

sentences.en: Not Romeo, Prince.
He was Mercutio's friend.
His crime only ended what the law would have ended anyway: Tybalt's life.

speaker: PRINCE
raw:
And for that offence
Immediately we do exile him hence.
I have an interest in your hate’s proceeding,
My blood for your rude brawls doth lie a-bleeding.
But I’ll amerce you with so strong a fine
That you shall all repent the loss of mine.
I will be deaf to pleading and excuses;
Nor tears nor prayers shall purchase out abuses.
Therefore use none. Let Romeo hence in haste,
Else, when he is found, that hour is his last.
Bear hence this body, and attend our will.
Mercy but murders, pardoning those that kill.

sentences.en: For that crime, we exile him: he must leave this city at once.
Your hatred has hurt me personally.
My blood is bleeding because of your rude fight.
But I will fine you so heavily that you will all be sorry for my loss.
I will not listen to pleas or excuses.
Neither tears nor prayers will change the punishment.
So do not use them.
Let Romeo leave here quickly.
If he is found, that hour will be his last.
Take this body away.
Follow my orders.
Mercy that forgives killers only causes more murder.

raw: Exeunt.
